templates.choose_when: Use when the causal route is the lesson and each arrow has a defensible meaning.
templates.choose_something_else_when: Use real UI for exact interaction steps; do not use an outcome card as evidence that execution succeeded.

templates.choose_when: Use when the distinction among source classes matters and they share a real destination.
templates.choose_something_else_when: Use a list for unrelated items; label search/query/tool access rather than implying data ingestion.
transcript_patterns: These inputs differ, but they contribute to the same {{shared_layer}}.

templates.choose_when: Use when the viewer needs a definition before a mechanism or example.
templates.choose_something_else_when: Do not use a logo reveal to explain an internal architecture.

templates.choose_when: Use after a capability needs a tangible demonstration.
templates.choose_something_else_when: Use genuine product footage for actual execution; label invented chat examples as illustrative.
transcript_patterns: From that answer, you can {{next_action}}, subject to {{constraint}}.

templates.choose_when: Use when a boundary constrains an otherwise understandable flow.
templates.choose_something_else_when: A shield alone does not explain a permission model; identify the actor, scope and enforcement point.

templates.choose_when: Use when the products are peers with shared foundations.
templates.choose_something_else_when: Do not turn peer products into an execution pipeline or imply dependency from card depth.
transcript_patterns: These are different ways to use {{shared_capability}}, depending on {{user_job}}.

templates.relationship: question → plausible but wrong asset → wrong answer
templates.choose_when: Use when the failure is asset authority or relevance rather than arithmetic.
templates.choose_something_else_when: Use a definition comparison for metric ambiguity; avoid showing a random table when the problem is a formula.
transcript_patterns: It finds {{candidate}}, but that is not the {{trusted_definition_or_source}} used by {{owner}}.

templates.relationship: same term → missing rule → changed interpretation
templates.choose_when: Use when scope, exclusions or semantics cause ambiguity.
templates.choose_something_else_when: Use a source-authority graphic for choosing among tables; do not imply a definition alone repairs stale data.
transcript_patterns: When we say {{metric}}, we mean {{definition}}, including {{included_population}} and excluding {{excluded_population}}.

templates.choose_when: Use when time or organizational change breaks relevance.
templates.choose_something_else_when: A stale icon does not prove freshness checks exist; show the changed reference and its consequence.
transcript_patterns: The {{entity}} was {{change}}, so the previous {{reference}} is now unreliable.

templates.relationship: broken route → missing context → repaired route
templates.choose_when: Use after a concrete failure has established why the missing context matters.
templates.choose_something_else_when: Do not promise that context fixes all data-quality, model or authorization failures.
transcript_patterns: The missing piece is {{business_context}}, which tells {{system}} how to interpret {{asset}}.

templates.choose_when: Use when placement in the larger system is part of the explanation.
templates.choose_something_else_when: Use a standalone example when the architecture adds no relevant context.
transcript_patterns: At a high level, {{system}} contains {{components}}. Let’s focus on {{component}}.
{{component}} sits between {{upstream}} and {{downstream}} and is responsible for {{responsibility}}.

templates.choose_when: Use for a real parent, containment or grouping relationship.
templates.choose_something_else_when: Use equal peer cards when no parent-child relationship exists; do not invent permission inheritance.
transcript_patterns: Start with {{definition_object}}, add {{context_object}}, then organize them into {{domain}}.

templates.choose_when: Use when the lesson is how evidence contributes contextual clues.
templates.choose_something_else_when: Do not represent learned signals as certified definitions or guaranteed truth.
transcript_patterns: When people {{work_action}}, they leave {{signal}} that helps {{system}} infer {{context}}.

templates.relationship: candidate context → ranking criteria → relevant context
templates.choose_when: Use when relevance or prioritization is the causal lesson.
templates.choose_something_else_when: A generic node graph does not explain ranking; name the criteria and avoid inventing numerical weights.
transcript_patterns: Not every {{candidate}} is equally useful; {{ranking_rule}} changes which ones matter for {{question}}.

templates.choose_when: Use for comparable measured data with a credible evaluation scope.
templates.choose_something_else_when: Do not transfer source benchmark values to another product or imply universal results from one evaluation.

templates.choose_when: Use when superficially similar access paths have different semantics.
templates.choose_something_else_when: A collage of logos cannot distinguish retrieval from execution or ingestion.
transcript_patterns: Finding an existing {{document}} differs from calculating {{answer}} over live {{data}}.

templates.choose_when: Use when the actual visible product interaction supports the claim.
templates.choose_something_else_when: Do not fabricate UI or infer availability beyond the visible source version.

templates.choose_when: Use when the permission boundary or action route matters.
templates.choose_something_else_when: Compatibility logos are not proof of authorization or successful execution.
transcript_patterns: {{action}} is allowed for {{allowed_scope}} and denied for {{denied_scope}}.

templates.choose_when: Use when equal conceptual rank is the lesson.
templates.choose_something_else_when: Use a timeline when order matters and a hierarchy when one item contains another.
transcript_patterns: There are three distinct concerns: {{concern_a}}, {{concern_b}} and {{concern_c}}.

templates.choose_when: Use when delegation or ownership is a real relationship in the supported system.
templates.choose_something_else_when: Use an input map for context sources; do not present source connectors as subordinate agents.
transcript_patterns: Each {{specialist}} receives {{inputs}} and can use {{resources}} within {{scope}}.

templates.choose_when: Use for a real ordered process with useful current-step context.
templates.choose_something_else_when: Use peer cards for unordered considerations; a rail is not a promise about calendar duration.
transcript_patterns: Start with {{team_and_workflow}}, define {{benchmark}}, measure {{baseline}}, then connect {{sources}} and iterate.

templates.choose_when: Use when scanning the whole recommendation set helps orientation.
templates.choose_something_else_when: Do not fade inactive text below legibility or replace the list with unrelated slides.

templates.choose_when: Use for a short framing or recap phrase.
templates.choose_something_else_when: Use a diagram when the mechanism needs explanation; a floating word is insufficient.

templates.choose_when: Use for a real structural transition.
templates.choose_something_else_when: A chapter title is navigation, not an explanatory mechanism.

templates.choose_when: Use when exact interaction or observed execution is central.
templates.choose_something_else_when: Illustrative diagrams cannot verify real execution. Keep reference UI separate from generated conceptual graphics.
transcript_patterns: To verify {{claim}}, look at {{visible_evidence}} in the product.
